contract.cellFormula: EVIDENCE_KINDS.length (9, declared at e2e/fixtures/gmTwoPlayerEvidence.ts:42-52) x EVIDENCE_ROLES.length (3, declared at :61-65)
contract.rolesNote: EVIDENCE_ROLES (:61-65) are byte-identical to ROLES in e2e/fixtures/gmTwoPlayerCampaign.ts:13, which is what every fixture client's `client.role` carries (:133). Any OTHER role string passed to write() is recorded as an entry but matches NO matrix cell.

howFinalizeDecidesCompleteness.collector: openEvidenceBundle(runId, runtimeRoot) at :219-279 keeps an in-memory `entries: IEvidenceEntry[]`; write() at :231-252 pushes one entry per artifact after assertNoSecrets() and guards.assertRunOwnedPath().
howFinalizeDecidesCompleteness.matrixWalk: listMissingEvidenceCells(entries) at :143-158 builds a Set of `${kind}\0${role}` from the captured entries and walks EVIDENCE_KINDS x EVIDENCE_ROLES, returning every absent pair. Presence is exact string equality on BOTH kind and role.
howFinalizeDecidesCompleteness.gate: finalize(environment, options) at :256-278: if absent.length > 0 AND options?.allowIncompleteEvidence !== true, it throws EvidenceBundleError('EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE', `missing cells: ${formatMissingCells(absent)}`, absent) and writes NO manifest.json. Otherwise it writes manifest.json with { runId, environment, captured: entries, missing } to a run-owned path.
howFinalizeDecidesCompleteness.escapeHatch: IFinalizeOptions.allowIncompleteEvidence: true (:103-105) is opt-in, never a default. Every live strict row on main passes it.
howFinalizeDecidesCompleteness.recordMissingIsNotACell: recordMissing(kind, role, why) at :253-255 pushes onto a SEPARATE `missing` array that is written into the manifest but is NOT consulted by listMissingEvidenceCells. Declaring a hole does not fill a cell and does not open the gate.
howFinalizeDecidesCompleteness.writeApiIsStringOnly: write(kind, role, name, body: string) at :174-179. There is NO binary/Buffer path on baseline. The body also passes assertNoSecrets() against four SECRET_PATTERNS at :115-120.

binaryArtifactDecision.problem: Two of the nine kinds (screenshot, trace) are binary. The bundle's only writer takes a string.

optionA.name: base64 into the existing string writer
optionA.secretScanSafety: provably safe - all four SECRET_PATTERNS require a quote character or whitespace, and the base64 alphabet (A-Za-z0-9+/=) contains neither, so a bare base64 body can never match
optionA.objection: the letter says the per-run directory SHALL CONTAIN screenshots and a trace. A .b64 file is not a screenshot, and a multi-megabyte base64 trace is a poor artifact.
optionA.verdict: rejected - easy fix, not the correct one
